title.rendered: I Believed, Therefore I Spoke: The Spirit of Faith | How to Declare Like Jesus Did, Day 5

excerpt.rendered: Paul calls the link between belief and speech “the same spirit of faith.” Day 5 teaches that real faith does not stay silent, it is a spirit that speaks.

content.rendered:
Faith is not a feeling that keeps its mouth shut. It is a spirit, the kind that cannot stop speaking what it believes.

The Gospel For Today | Thursday, October 22, 2026 | How to Declare Like Jesus Did, Day 5

Today’s Scripture

“And since we have the same spirit of faith, according to what is written, ‘I believed and therefore I spoke,’ we also believe and therefore speak.”
2 Corinthians 4:13 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Paul is quoting Psalm 116:10. The psalmist had been through affliction, had tasted deliverance, and had learned the pattern: he believed, therefore he spoke. In the NKJV, 2 Corinthians 4:13 names it “the same spirit of faith.” The AMPC expands it: “Yet we have the same spirit of faith as he had who wrote, I have believed, and therefore I have spoken. We too believe, and therefore we speak.” The TPT says, “We have the same Spirit of faith that is described in the Scriptures when it says, ‘First I believed, then I spoke in faith.’ So we also first believe, then speak in faith.”

There is a divine order here. Belief is the root, speech is the fruit, and the two share one spirit. You cannot have New Testament faith without New Testament speech. In Lagos, a believer who truly trusts the Lord for a promotion will not spend the week telling his colleagues he is finished. In London, a mother who truly trusts God for her son does not join every conversation that writes him off. In Manila, Nairobi and São Paulo, a congregation praying for revival learns, over time, to speak like a revived people before the fire falls. Belief that cannot find its voice is still immature belief.

Jesus pressed this point until it was unavoidable: “Whoever says to this mountain, ‘Be removed and be cast into the sea,’ and does not doubt in his heart, but believes that those things he says will be done, he will have whatever he says” (Mark 11:23). Notice the words. Not “whoever thinks” or “whoever hopes”, whoever says. The spirit of faith is a speaking spirit, because faith is agreement with God, and agreement requires a voice.

This is also where many believers get stuck. We fear sounding presumptuous. We fear being proven wrong. But humility is not silence; humility is agreement with God against our fear. If God has said it, we are not being bold to say it too, we are being obedient. The spirit of faith does not wait until it feels brave. It opens its mouth and discovers courage along the way.

The Pattern of Declaration

Acknowledge. Faith and speech share one spirit. If you believe God, your tongue will eventually show it. If your tongue cannot show it, your heart has not yet fully settled.

Personalise. Ask the Holy Spirit which promise you have been believing silently and need to begin speaking. Silence can be reverent; it can also be unbelief dressed in modesty.

Proclaim. Begin to say what you have been believing. Say it in prayer. Say it out loud when you are alone. Say it when the opposite is true. The spirit of faith is a speaking spirit.

Declaration

I declare and acknowledge that I share the same spirit of faith with the psalmist, with Paul, and with the apostles. I believe, and therefore I speak. I will not carry my faith in silence. I will not whisper what God has shouted over my life. From this day I speak what I have believed. I say what the Word says about my body, my family, my work, and my future. My faith has a voice. My faith has a tongue. My faith has courage. My mountains hear me, because I am not doubting in my heart. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
